subject: Intermittent egress failures from customer private VPC — SG / egress-policy mismatch
messages:
From: Rita Shah <rita.shah@acme-retail.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent 502s from our private deployment to backend pool

Hi Markus / Marissa,

We're seeing intermittent 502/connection resets from the Acme private deployment that started after we rolled out an egress policy change this morning. Symptoms: some requests to our on-prem order processor time out or get a TCP reset; other connections succeed. Failures happen roughly 1 in 20 requests and appear to correlate with larger payloads (~>1.5KB).

Net ops (cc'd: Tomasz) have pulled some tcpdump segments and an ACL export. Attaching a short pcap and the current security group dump. Can you triage? We're in EU region and this is affecting peak traffic windows.

Attachments: packet_capture_segment.pcap (5MB), security_group_rules.txt

Thanks — we need a temporary mitigation ASAP (rate-limiting? fallback?).

— Rita
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Retail

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Rita Shah <rita.shah@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s from our private deployment to backend pool

Thanks Rita — escalating to our network infra team. Jonas / Hannah, can you pick this up? Please confirm: Acme's egress policy change time and the exact subnets impacted. Also capture the 5xx response headers from the Redwood side (we'll want token-level correlation).

Short asks for triage:
- Full pcap (we received a 10s slice; need three minutes spanning a failure and success)
- Routing table snapshot from the customer VPC and our peering appliance (route-table-snapshot.txt would be helpful)
- Confirm whether Acme enabled MTU clamping or changed NAT behavior earlier today

Rita — temporary mitigation options: pin to a fallback egress path (if available) or turn on prefix-preserving SNAT for that backend. We'll advise after initial triage.

— Markus
Sr. Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rita Shah <rita.shah@acme-retail.com>, Tomasz Kowalski <tk@networks.example.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s from our private deployment to backend pool — initial triage

Team — quick triage notes (attached: packet_capture_segment.pcap, route-table-snapshot.txt, security_group_rules.txt):

1) Observed behavior in pcap: repeated TCP 3-way handshake completes, then for sessions carrying larger payloads we see MSS/Fragmentation indications followed by RST from the customer subnet. On successful sessions the path MTU negotiation occurs differently (DF bit cleared). Patterns point at PMTU/fragmentation interaction plus a stateful firewall that drops fragments.

2) Route snapshot: route for 10.240.0.0/16 from our peering appliance alternates between two next-hops (vxlan-gw-a / vxlan-gw-b) depending on source. There's asymmetric egress — return traffic sometimes transits the other gateway which applies a different security-group/ACL set (see rules: gw-b has stricter drop policies for non-established fragments).

3) Security group dump: Acme's recent egress policy locked down ephemeral ports on gw-b and tightened a rule that inadvertently rejects packets with 'non-established' state (fragments). That aligns with failures on larger payloads where fragmentation would be involved.

Immediate mitigations tested: we applied a temporary SNAT rule at the peering appliance to normalize source IPs via gw-a for a subset of flows — that reduced failures in the test window.

Proposed next steps:
- Ask Acme to relax fragment handling on gw-b (short term) OR enable MTU clamping at the VPC edge to avoid fragmentation.
- Make the temporary SNAT change permanent for the affected prefix while we roll a config fix.
- Schedule controlled repro with tcpdump across both gateways to prove the fix end-to-end.

I'll prepare a short runbook for rollback in case of regressions. Jonas
Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Tomasz Kowalski <tk@networks.example.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rita Shah <rita.shah@acme-retail.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s from our private deployment to backend pool — firewall side

Jonas, Markus — thanks for the quick analysis. Confirming from Acme ops: earlier today we pushed a hardening change on gw-b that tightened fragment handling (we expected no fragmentation due to 1500 MTU, but some clients do set DF unset). We can temporarily relax that ACL for the affected prefix and enable MTU clamp on the VXLAN to 1400 for a short validation window.

Proposed action plan (we can do these in a maintenance window tonight):
- Relax 'drop non-established-fragment' ACL on gw-b for 10.240.128.0/24 and monitor for 2hrs.
- Apply MTU clamp 1400 on VTEP interfaces for the Acme VXLAN.
- Keep the temporary SNAT at Redwood side as a safety net during rollout.

If Redwood prefers, we can also run an A/B where half the sessions use gw-a and half gw-b to validate parity.

— Tomasz
Network Ops, Acme Retail (via Networks Example)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Rita Shah <rita.shah@acme-retail.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 502s from our private deployment to backend pool — post-mitigation update

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps.

What we changed:
- Acme relaxed the fragment-drop ACL on gw-b for 10.240.128.0/24 (Tomasz applied).
- Acme enabled MTU clamp to 1400 on the VXLAN VTEPs for the Acme tenant.
- Redwood kept the temporary SNAT mapping on our peering appliance for 72 hours as a fall-back; we will remove after a successful validation window.

Result: failure rate dropped from ~5% -> 0.1% during peak testing. We observed no new RSTs or 502s in a 4-hour storm test. Attached are the verification pcaps and the final route-table-snapshot.

Action items:
- (Acme) Please keep the ACL change in place until we validate for 72 hours, then revert to a targeted rule if you prefer.
- (Redwood) We'll add an entry to our private-deploy runbook documenting asymmetric-gateway SNAT as an emergency mitigation and a checklist for MTU clamp tests.
- Schedule a 30-minute postmortem with stakeholders next week to discuss long-term options (BFD to detect next-hop churn? strict route pinning?). Marissa, can you coordinate invites?

Thanks for the quick coordination — this was a subtle interaction between MTU/fragmentation handling and per-gateway ACLs.

— Markus
Sr. Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: packet_capture_segment.pcap (validation slices), route-table-snapshot.txt, security_group_rules.txt
